engagement_background.objective: Choice Health at Home engaged Treya Partners to capture roughly $0.54-1.2 million in annual savings through strategic sourcing of key indirect and clinical-support spend categories, leveraging enterprise-wide purchasing power to boost EBITDA and stand up a best-in-class procurement process before July 2024.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Initial scope covers 12 categories—Fleet, Employee Benefits, Medical Supplies, Pharmacy, Medical Equipment, Temp Labor (Therapists and Nurses), Telecom (Data & Voice), Commercial Print, Copiers/MFPs, Office Supplies and IT Hardware—representing about $17.7 million in annual spend with 75-90 % addressability. Large direct-care areas (e.g., Doctors, Homecare Software, Hospice Services) and any categories not listed in Exhibit A are currently out of scope or on hold.
constraints_challenges: Supplier lack of responsiveness to data and usage requests, slowing baseline development
Incumbent supplier pushback requiring a unified ‘one-voice’ negotiation strategy
Risk of unauthorized “side conversations” with suppliers that could erode leverage
Limited stakeholder availability for data provision, interviews, and timely feedback
Aggressive five-to-six-month timeline to deliver savings and complete sourcing by July 2024
Incomplete or non-standardized usage and contract data; AP file required significant cleanup and mapping
Sensitivity around certain strategic suppliers where Choice may prefer to lead negotiations

procurement_environment.data_availability: Accounts-payable spend extract (~$39 M) available in Excel; no centralized contract repository; limited internal usage reporting—Treya must request line-item data directly from high-spend suppliers.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Duplicate vendor naming, unmapped GL lines and missing historical usage data; some suppliers unwilling or slow to provide 12-month histories, creating gaps in the baseline.
